solution: A full mesh links every device directly to every other device, so there is no single point of failure and traffic has many alternative paths, giving very high reliability; however, eight computers need 8 x 7 / 2 = 28 links and each device needs several network interfaces, so it is expensive and difficult to install and extend. A star connects every device to one central switch, so it needs only 9 cables, is cheap and easy to manage and extend, and a failed cable only affects one device; however, if the central switch fails the whole network stops. For a small practice with a limited budget a star is more appropriate, with reliability improved by keeping a spare switch rather than paying for a full mesh.

marking_points.criterion: Mesh: every device directly connected, alternative paths / no single point of failure, so highly reliable.
Mesh: many links/interfaces (e.g. 28 links for 8 devices), so high cost and complex to scale.
Star: cheap/simple, one cable per device to a central switch; a cable failure affects only one device.
Star: central switch is a single point of failure, with a justified recommendation for the practice.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept a correct link-count argument without the exact number. Accept recommending a star with a backup switch, or a reasoned case for mesh if cost is addressed.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 4 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.
